answer: Exit-bond resistance: each identity locks a bond refundable only after its history clears audit; early exit burns half, so sybils are cheap to mint, costly to shed, and cost(n) rises super-linearly per alias and coalition, since every exit lengthens one shared refund queue. Entrants pay; auditors earn fees from the forfeited pool each close. Auditor seats are random quorums whose standing decays without reviewing closes. Fail case: auditor collusion, blunted since seats carry non-transferable reputation; a tainted audit is a loud island of signal, its stain spreading like a delta to signers.
